cells.verb: letting yourself feel before you know what the feeling is about
cells.place: in the push toward what you're after
cells.ask: take one thing about this goal you've already settled and let it be felt again, as if for the first time — what comes back is a knowing that keeps getting truer instead of one that closes
cells.core: You're moving toward something and your heart is open while you move. That's not a contradiction, though it often gets treated like one — the direction is set and you're still available to what shows up along the way, before you've named it or decided what to do with it. You don't need the destination to be finished to feel where you are on the road to it. What comes next is optional, and it's a deepening rather than a correction: there's probably one piece of this you decided and stopped feeling. It could stand to be felt again. Not reconsidered — just met, open, the way you met the rest of it. The knowing you're carrying isn't done. It's the kind that keeps going.
cells.sheetLine: You're moving toward it with your heart still open — and the knowing isn't finished.

cells.tense: Future — bracing at something that hasn't arrived
cells.verb: feeling everything about where you're going before you've gotten there
cells.place: in the push toward what you're after
cells.ask: finish one thing all the way to done, chosen from where you actually stand rather than from what you dread, and let the finishing itself be the answer — what comes back is a knowing that keeps deepening instead of flooding
cells.core: You're wide open to a future that hasn't happened yet. Every version of how this goes is already landing in you — the win, the loss, the way they'll look at you — and you're feeling it all before any of it is real. The motion that was supposed to carry you there is getting swamped by what you're feeling about there. Direction can't hold under that much anticipation; it starts steering by dread instead of by choice. What helps isn't feeling less. It's finishing something. Take one piece that can actually be completed and complete it, on purpose, from the ground you're standing on today — and let it be done when it's done. A thing carried to its end gives the feeling somewhere to land that's real. The heart that opened to this will still be open. It'll just be open to what's here.
cells.sheetLine: You're feeling the whole future before you've moved an inch toward it.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at a door that's already behind you
cells.verb: shut to what you feel while you keep moving
cells.place: in the push toward what you're after
cells.ask: take one thing you've already brought into being and meet it today as though you'd never seen it — carry it fresh — and what comes back is a knowing that starts moving again instead of standing where it was
cells.core: You're still moving toward the goal. You're just not feeling anything about it. The direction got set and the heart closed behind it, and you're running on that earlier decision instead of on anything you're feeling now — the momentum is real, the destination is real, and nobody's home in it. The road doesn't hurt. It also doesn't mean anything. Trying to force feeling back into the push won't work; it's empty because it's cut off, not because it needs more effort. What helps is on the other end: something you've already made, already finished, already carried into the world. Go stand in front of it. Meet it as if you'd never seen it before — fresh, no verdict. Feeling tends to come back through what's done before it comes back through what's still being chased. Then the knowing starts to move again instead of staying where you left it.
cells.sheetLine: You're still pushing toward it. The feeling didn't come with you.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing
cells.place: in the push toward what you're after
cells.ask: about one choice you've been calling the obvious one, say 'this is how it feels right to me' — once, plainly — and let it sit without defending it; what comes back is a knowing you can admit to, which is the kind that gets to deepen
cells.core: Your heart is already in this. It's choosing the turns, deciding what's worth the push and what isn't, picking up on things before your reasons catch up — and you describe all of it as strategy. The smart move. The obvious call. The feeling is doing the steering and the credit is going to logic, which is a quiet kind of theft from yourself. There's no call to make it more than it is. Just smaller and truer. Pick one decision you've been calling obvious and say what's actually underneath it: this is how it felt right. Say it once, and don't argue for it afterward. Knowing that's allowed to be knowing — without a brief attached — lands on its own, and it keeps going. The kind that gets dressed up as a plan stops where the plan does.
cells.sheetLine: Your heart is already steering this. You keep calling it strategy.

flags.detail: "a while ago" — a cell knows no one's past
